Hello Voaters,

During my few days being a member of the Voat community, I noticed a few comments and threads from a couple users that complain about their posts being deleted. These users usually say their postings were deleted unjustly, that they were "censored," and quote Voat's well known slogan "the place where you can have your say." Well, today I am going to use a couple examples to show the difference between a post being deleted for breaking subverse rules, and a post being deleted for censorship.

Breaking Subverse Rules: If a post is deleted off of a certain subverse, it is most likely that post does not belong in that particular location. Most subverses set up specific rules to keep the subverse flowing smoothly and to prevent fighting and disorder within the page. These rules are set in place to keep the peace. These rules are NOT in place to tell you your opinion does not matter. If your opinion does not fit into the rules of a subverse, you are more than welcome to post your opinion in a more appropriate subverse, or create a new subverse entirely!

Censorship: Censorship on a site like Voat or Reddit occurs when an opinion or idea is not allowed anywhere on the website, regardless of placement. This usually occurs when the website does not want certain ideas or opinions to be known to other people in the community, and are banned even if the opinion or idea is placed in an appropriate place. Reddit banning ideas such as disliking overweight people and hiding information such as Ellen Pao's current lawsuit costs are examples of censorship.

Voat is a website that offers the freedom to create you own haven within their servers and spread your opinions and ideas (within legal limits). Please, respect the rules of subverses, and if you feel like your opinion does not fit, then make a subverse that makes your opinion fit.
There is a difference between censorship and breaking subverse rules
